title: Privacy
text:
Last updated: 13 August 2026
Raccoon Backgammon collects nothing. There is no account to create, no tracking, no analytics, no advertising, and no cookies.

title: Privacy
text:
Where the engine runs
The neural network runs in your browser. When you load the play or analyse page, your browser downloads the network’s weights once and evaluates positions locally on your own machine. Positions you play or paste are never transmitted to us — there is no server to transmit them to, and no game data leaves your device.

title: Privacy
text:
What the host can see
This site is static and served by GitHub Pages. Like any web host, GitHub receives the technical information your browser sends when requesting a page — IP address, user agent, and the URL requested — and may log it. That processing is GitHub’s, described in the GitHub Privacy Statement. We have no access to those logs and add no tracking of our own.

title: Privacy
text:
Email
If you email hello@raccoonbg.com we keep the message so we can reply. We do not add you to any mailing list — there isn’t one.

title: Privacy
text:
Your rights
Since we hold no personal data beyond correspondence you choose to send, there is normally nothing to access, correct or erase. If you have written to us and want that correspondence deleted, ask and we will delete it.
Data controller: Tekst og tal, CVR 34101302, Denmark — hello@raccoonbg.com.

title: Raccoon Backgammon
text: Backgammon’s strongest engines were built in the 1990s. Raccoon is a rebuild with the methods that have since transformed chess and Go — a deep residual network trained by large-scale distillation — and it runs entirely in your browser. No account, no server, nothing to install.

title: Raccoon Backgammon
text:
What it does

Play a full cubeless money game against the engine — full-size board.
Analyse any position: ranked candidate moves, cubeless equity, and the win/gammon/backgammon split — open the analyser.
Bring your own positions with XGID import and export, the format XG and GNU Backgammon already speak.

Everything happens on your machine: the network’s weights are downloaded once and evaluated locally, so nothing you play is ever sent anywhere.

title: Raccoon Backgammon
text:
How strong is it
Scored on the BGSage money benchmark — 14,693 checker decisions with rollout-quality references. PR is mean move-selection error × 500; lower is better.








Engine
Compute per decision
PR (14,693 decisions)




GNU Backgammon, 2-ply full-width search
~1.3 s
0.56


Raccoon, single network evaluation
~10 ms
0.95


GNU Backgammon, single network evaluation
~10 ms
2.14



At equal cost Raccoon’s checker play is well past GNU Backgammon’s own network, and it has closed most of the distance to GNU Backgammon’s 2-ply search while doing no search at all. In direct play it wins +0.046 ± 0.005 points per game against GNU Backgammon at 0-ply over 6,000 games — measured with variance-reduced rollouts, which read the same games seven times more precisely than counting points does.
The engine in your browser is the measured engine, not a cut-down version of it: the exported network scores PR 0.9500 on the benchmark against 0.9498 for the PyTorch checkpoint it came from.
The honest caveat: this is checker play only, cubeless. The doubling cube — half of competitive backgammon — is the next milestone.

title: Analyse a position
text:
The analyser needs JavaScript and WebAssembly. The same engine runs in a terminal.

Bring a position. Paste an XGID from XG, GNU Backgammon or Backgammon Galaxy and the board will load it; edit the board by hand if you prefer; copy the XGID back out when you are done.
What the numbers mean. Every legal play is ranked by cubeless equity in points, from the perspective of the player on roll, together with the probabilities of winning plain, with a gammon, and with a backgammon — read straight from the network’s six-outcome value head. Equity differences are shown against the best play, which is the same quantity error rates are built from.
Cube decisions are not analysed. The cube fields of an XGID are read and displayed but not evaluated: this engine is cubeless for now.

title: Changelog
section: 2026-08 — A doubles bug worth 0.033 points per game
text:
2026-08 — A doubles bug worth 0.033 points per game

On a double, the engine was choosing its four half-moves two at a time rather than optimising the turn as a whole. It cost 0.062 points on the one doubles turn in six where the difference mattered. Fixing the search — with no change to the network — took the margin over GNU Backgammon at 0-ply from +0.013 to +0.046 ± 0.005 points per game. How it was found. The browser engine plays the fixed way.

title: Changelog
section: 2026-08 — First head-to-head win over GNU Backgammon
text:
2026-08 — First head-to-head win over GNU Backgammon

Variance-reduced rollouts put exp018-ep22 ahead of GNU Backgammon at 0-ply over 6,000 games — the first time a Raccoon network has been shown to beat the teacher it was distilled from in actual play. The plain average over the same games settles nothing at ±0.035; the variance reduction is worth about 55× as many games. Method and result.

title: Changelog
text:
2026-08 — 40M-position distillation

Scaling 2-ply distillation from 8M to 40M positions cut move-selection error from PR 2.16 to 0.93 and brought value accuracy to teacher level, with no trade-off across game plans. Write-up.

Every experiment behind these releases is published in full, including the ones that failed, at research.raccoonbg.com.

title: The engine
text: The engine that plays you in the browser is the same one you can download and run yourself. It is MIT-licensed and written in Python and PyTorch, with game rules from OpenSpiel.

title: The engine
text:
Install
git clone https://github.com/lassehjorthmadsen/raccoon.git
cd raccoon
make setup          # editable install with dev dependencies
make test           # run the test suite
make play           # play against Raccoon in the terminal

title: The engine
text:
What the network is







Architecture
10-block, 256-channel residual network — 11.9M parameters


Input
A (26, 2, 12) tensor: checker planes, bar/borne-off/dice broadcasts, and handcrafted pip, blot, anchor and contact features


Value head
Six mutually exclusive outcomes — win, gammon, backgammon, each way — from which cubeless equity follows


Move selection
0-ply value lookahead: every legal play is evaluated in one batched forward pass, no search


Training
Supervised distillation of 40M positions labelled by GNU Backgammon’s 2-ply search

title: The engine
text:
Strength
Scored on the BGSage money benchmark — 14,693 checker decisions with rollout-quality cubeless-equity references. PR is mean move-selection error × 500; lower is better.








Engine

~1.3 s

~10 ms
0.95


GNU Backgammon, single evaluation (0-ply)
~10 ms
2.14



In head-to-head play against GNU Backgammon at 0-ply, Raccoon wins +0.046 ± 0.005 points per game over 6,000 cubeless money games scored with variance-reduced rollouts.
Two thirds of that margin came from fixing the search, not the network: on a double the engine used to pick its four half-moves two at a time instead of optimising the whole turn, which cost 0.033 points per game. The browser engine optimises doubles jointly, like the measured one.
The browser runs this network exported to ONNX. That exported file was scored on the same benchmark, at the same sample size, and lands on the same number (PR 0.9500 for the ONNX file versus 0.9498 for the PyTorch checkpoint, n = 14,693) — so the engine you play here is the engine that was measured, not a reduced version of it.
What it does not do yet: the doubling cube. Play here and in the CLI is cubeless money game. Cube handling is the next milestone.

title: The engine
text:
Embedding it
The engine speaks the Raccoon Game Protocol, a UCI-style line protocol over stdin/stdout intended for analysis GUIs. See raccoon/protocol/rgp.py and the architecture notes. If you are building a tool and want to embed Raccoon, get in touch.

title: Play Raccoon
text:
The board needs JavaScript and WebAssembly. The same engine runs in a terminal if you would rather not use a browser.

How to play. Roll, then click a checker and its destination. The engine replies immediately and shows what it thought of your move. Everything runs on your machine — the network is downloaded once and evaluated locally.
Rules in force. Cubeless money game: gammons and backgammons count double and triple, and there is no doubling cube yet. The engine picks its move by evaluating every legal play with one forward pass of the network — the same 0-ply value lookahead the published strength numbers measure.

title: Team
text: Raccoon is built by Tekst og tal, a one-person research and development company registered in Denmark (CVR 34101302).

title: Team
text:
How we work
Everything is measured, and everything is published. Each experiment states one hypothesis, fixes one primary metric before the run, and reports every checkpoint against it with sample sizes and confidence intervals. The write-ups include the experiments that failed, the conclusions later retracted, and the measurement bugs found in our own evaluation code. In a domain where effect sizes are small and noise is large, a result without its error bar is not a result.
The code is open. The engine, training pipelines and evaluation harnesses are MIT-licensed and public. Game rules come from OpenSpiel; every line of the machine learning and search code is written from scratch.
Training runs on Google Cloud — preemptible GPU instances for network training, Cloud Storage for datasets and checkpoints.
